gaps.sentence: The country is facing a serious ___ crisis.
gaps.hint: connected with money, trade and industry
gaps.explanation: 'Economic' means connected with the economy; 'economical' means saving money.
'It's' is short for 'it is' or 'it has'; here it means 'it has been raining'. The possessive is 'its'.

gaps.sentence: Tax is calculated on your total annual ___.
gaps.hint: all the money you receive from every source
gaps.explanation: 'Income' is all the money you receive from work, investments, rent and so on during a period.

gaps.sentence: They managed to ___ the champions in the final.
gaps.explanation: 'Beat' takes the opponent as object (beat the champions); 'win' takes the game or prize.

gaps.hint: you ___ a match, but ___ the other team
gaps.explanation: 'Win' takes the game or prize as object (win a match); 'beat/defeat' take the opponent as object.

gaps.sentence: The Sahara is the largest hot ___ in the world.
gaps.explanation: 'Desert' is a dry region with little rain; 'dessert' is the sweet course of a meal.

gaps.sentence: Pens, envelopes and paper are sold in the ___ department.
gaps.explanation: 'Stationery' means writing materials; 'stationary' is an adjective meaning not moving.

gaps.sentence: I start my new ___ at the hospital on Monday.
gaps.hint: a single, countable position of employment
gaps.explanation: 'Job' is countable — one particular position; 'work' is uncountable and cannot follow 'a new'.
